    # assignment of $script:MtRoles not persisting into the Pester test-execution
    # context (the cause of the MT.1020 NullReferenceException). See Get-MtRoleInfo.
    Initialize-MtRoleDefinition

content.text:
It's not stuck. It's making a few hundred slow Graph calls one after another.

**Why it takes so long:**

1. [Test.CIS.M365.1.1.1.ps1](../tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.1.1.1.ps1) picks every role whose name contains "Administrator", plus Global Reader. That's about 80–100 built-in roles, and it passes all of their IDs to `Get-MtRoleMember`.
2. `Get-MtRoleMember` calls `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId $RoleId -ExpandPrincipal`. That helper sends **one request per role**, filtered on `roleDefinitionId`.
3. On a P2 or Governance tenant, it does that **twice per role**: once to `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` and once to `roleEligibilityScheduleInstances`. Both use `$expand=principal`, and the PIM schedule-instance endpoints often take 1–2 seconds per call.
4. So that's roughly 160–200 calls, none of them batched or run in parallel. Each URI has its own filter, so the cache doesn't save anything within this check either. At that rate it adds up to about 3–6 minutes. Expanding the members of each role-assignable group adds a bit more.

The final user lookup (`-UniqueId`) is batched 20 at a time, so it isn't the cause.

**Proposed fix:** when the helper gets more than a few role IDs, make one unfiltered (paged) request for active assignments and one for eligible assignments, then filter by `roleDefinitionId` in PowerShell. That cuts the calls from about 180 to a few pages, and other checks can reuse the cached result. It would also speed up the other CIS tests and MT checks that go through `Get-MtRoleMember` with many roles. The fix goes in [Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1](internal/services/entra/Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1).

Your current run should finish on its own; it's working through the calls, not hung.
Yes, fix it

# Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment pack

The [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) is Microsoft's free tool that checks a tenant
against Microsoft's Zero Trust guidance, across identity, devices, network, data, AI and security operations, and
says how to fix what it finds.
[Try the demo report](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment/demo) to see what it covers.

This pack runs the assessment from Maester and shows each of its results in the Maester report, next to Maester's
own checks. It ships with Maester and runs only when you ask for it.

Each result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the assessment's title, risk
level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged `ZeroTrust` and
`ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

Maester also places each result under the product, feature and security area it is about, such as Entra ID and
Conditional Access, and lists the MITRE ATT&CK techniques its control addresses, so assessment results appear
beside Maester's own checks in the report's product, area and ATT&CK views. The assessment does not record these,
so Maester keeps the mapping in the pack's `taxonomy.json`.

## Report an issue with a test

Microsoft writes and maintains the assessment's tests. If a test's result, text or remediation looks wrong, raise
it in [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/issues). Problems with
running the pack from Maester go to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues).

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

The assessment runs in its own PowerShell process, so Maester signs in there for you. After an interactive
`Connect-Maester` you sign in a second time, in the browser. Without a browser, for example over SSH, set
`ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "UseDeviceCode": true }` in `maester-config.json`.

### Sign in as a service principal

In a pipeline, or anywhere nobody can sign in, connect Maester to Graph app-only with a certificate. The
assessment uses the same app and certificate, found by its thumbprint in the certificate store. A client secret, a
managed identity or workload identity federation is enough for Maester's own tests, but the assessment signs in
app-only only with a certificate.

```powershell
Import-Module ZeroTrustAssessment
Get-ZtGraphScope    # the Graph application permissions to give the app

Connect-MgGraph -ClientId <app id> -TenantId <tenant id> -CertificateThumbprint <thumbprint> -NoWelcome
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -NonInteractive
```

To leave out the assessment's Azure, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and SharePoint tests, which need extra
roles for the app, set `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "Service": ["Graph"] }`.

content.text:
After the fix, CIS.M365.1.1.1 reads role assignments the way the Zero Trust Assessment does. The two checks still disagree on which roles count as administrative. ZTA's check for this is `Test-Assessment.21814` in Microsoft's ZeroTrustAssessment module (3.1.0, installed on this Mac); our pack only runs that module.

**How each one gets its data**

| | ZTA 21814 | CIS.M365.1.1.1 (after the fix) |
|---|---|---|
| Role assignments | Exported once, unfiltered: `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` (`assignmentType eq 'Assigned'`) plus `roleEligibilityScheduleInstances` on P2, otherwise `roleAssignments`. Uses beta and `$expand=principal($select=id)`. | The same endpoints and filter, unfiltered and cached. Uses v1.0 and expands the full principal. |
| Which roles count | Graph's own `isPrivileged` flag on each role definition | Name contains "Administrator", plus Global Reader |
| Group-assigned roles | Expands members of privileged groups during the export | `Get-MtGroupMember` for each assigned group |
| User sync status | Exports **every user** (`$top=999`, with `onPremisesSyncEnabled`) once and joins in DuckDB | Looks up only the admin users by ID, in batches of 20 |
| Missing data | Returns **Investigate** when a user record or a role's privilege flag is missing | Throws an error |

Before the fix, CIS sent two requests per role, about 180 one after another. That was the whole reason for the 5 minutes. ZTA made two calls, which is what we do now.

**Where they still differ**

- **Role scope (the main gap).** Graph's `isPrivileged` flag covers fewer roles than the name match. It leaves out admin roles that can't change security settings, and it includes some roles without "Administrator" in the name, such as Privileged Authentication Administrator and some readers. On the same tenant, a hybrid user in, say, Teams Administrator fails CIS but passes ZTA. CIS 1.1.1 asks about administrative accounts, so I'd keep the CIS scope as it is.
- **Fetching every user.** ZTA's approach pays off because about 20 of its tests share that one export. For a single Maester check, the targeted ID lookup is cheaper. Keep ours.
- **Inconclusive results.** ZTA's Investigate result is gentler than our error, but both refuse to pass on incomplete data. No change needed.

**Two loose ends I noticed**

- **Duplicate checks.** `CISA.MS.AAD.7.3` checks the same thing as CIS.M365.1.1.1, but only for Global Administrators. ZTA's `AlsoCheckedBy` links to the CISA check and not to CIS.M365.1.1.1, even though the CIS check is the closer match to ZTA's broader privileged-roles scope. That mapping is kept by hand in `build/zta/`.
- **Another slow ZTA check.** ZTA's own `Test-Assessment.21816` still makes one `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` call per member and role, the same slow pattern we just removed. If a ZTA run drags there, that's a fix for Microsoft's repository, not ours.

function Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the users that hold any of the given directory roles, with whether each is synced from on-premises.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads the members of the roles with Get-MtRoleMember (active and eligible, including the members of
    role-assignable groups), keeps the users, and reads id, displayName and onPremisesSyncEnabled for each.

    Which roles to pass is the caller's decision: each benchmark defines its own set of privileged roles,
    and this helper only does the Graph reads they share.

    Throws when Graph does not return a user, or returns one without onPremisesSyncEnabled, so a check
    cannot pass without evaluating every member. Returns nothing when the roles have no user members.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' | Where-Object onPremisesSyncEnabled

    Returns the Global Administrators that are synced from on-premises.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # The IDs of the role definitions whose user members to return.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [guid[]] $RoleId
    )

    $members = @(Get-MtRoleMember -RoleId $RoleId)
    $userIds = @($members | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' } |
            ForEach-Object { [string]$_.id } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    if ($userIds.Count -eq 0) { return }

    Write-Verbose "Reading onPremisesSyncEnabled for $($userIds.Count) role members"
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId $userIds -Select id, displayName, onPremisesSyncEnabled)

    $returnedUserIds = @($users | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.id })
    $missingUserIds = @($userIds | Where-Object { $_ -notin $returnedUserIds })
    if ($missingUserIds.Count -gt 0) {
        throw "Microsoft Graph did not return user details for all role members. Missing user IDs: $($missingUserIds -join ', ')."
    }

    $missingSyncStatusIds = @($users | Where-Object { $_.PSObject.Properties.Name -notcontains 'onPremisesSyncEnabled' } |
            ForEach-Object { [string]$_.id })
    if ($missingSyncStatusIds.Count -gt 0) {
        throw "Microsoft Graph did not return onPremisesSyncEnabled for role members: $($missingSyncStatusIds -join ', ')."
    }

    $users
}

content.text:
All three are done; nothing is committed yet.

**1. No dependency on ZTA.** The speed fix lives only in [Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1](powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1). It reads Graph through `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` and the session cache, just like before. It never touches the ZeroTrustAssessment module, its DuckDB database or `vwRole`. ZTA only came up to compare how the two read the data.

**2. ZTA.21814 now lists CIS.M365.1.1.1.** I added it to `AlsoCheckedBy` in [taxonomy.json](packs/zero-trust-assessment/taxonomy.json), next to `CISA.MS.AAD.7.3`. Then I regenerated `catalog.json` with `Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1` against the installed module (3.1.0, the same version the catalog already uses). The only change in the catalog is that one line.

**3. Shared Graph lookup, separate role definitions.** The new internal helper [Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus.ps1](powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus.ps1) takes `-RoleId`. It reads the role members (active, eligible and members of role-assignable groups), keeps the users, and looks up `onPremisesSyncEnabled` for each in batches. It throws if Graph leaves out a user or the sync field. It doesn't decide which roles count; each check passes its own:
- [CIS.M365.1.1.1](tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.1.1.1.ps1): every role named "*Administrator*", plus Global Reader. Its report text is unchanged.
- [CISA.MS.AAD.7.3](tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.7.3.ps1): Global Administrator only, as before. It now also gets the "missing user" checks and no longer makes an extra `Get-MtRole` call.

New unit tests are in [Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus.Tests.ps1](powershell/tests/functions/Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus.Tests.ps1). In the full run (`./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`), 6,969 of 6,974 tests pass. The new helper caused two analyzer failures; I fixed the attribute that caused them, and the three changed files now pass the analyzer with no warnings. I re-ran the helper and CIS 1.1.1 tests (8 passed), but not the full run. The other three failures come from files this work doesn't touch:
- `Invoke-MtNativePlan.ps1` trips the analyzer's unused-parameter rule (two failures).
- `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails. That's probably because the ZTA module is installed on this Mac, but I haven't confirmed it.

**One thing to decide.** SCuBA's MS.AAD.7.3 covers "privileged users". As far as I recall, ScubaGear's default list of privileged roles goes beyond Global Administrator to include Privileged Role Administrator, User Administrator, Exchange and SharePoint Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, and Application and Cloud Application Administrator. I haven't checked that list against SCuBA's source, and I left the scope at Global Administrator only, as you asked. With the shared helper, widening it would mean changing only the role IDs the CISA check passes.
Yes, own branch

## 📑 Description

CIS.M365.1.1.1 (Ensure Administrative accounts are cloud-only) took more than five minutes on a live tenant.

**Cause.** The check asks `Get-MtRoleMember` for every role whose name contains "Administrator", plus Global Reader (about 100 roles). `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment` sent one request per role, filtered on `roleDefinitionId`. On P2 and Governance tenants it sent two: one to `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` and one to `roleEligibilityScheduleInstances`, both with `$expand=principal`. That came to close to 200 PIM calls, sent one after another, and the cache could not help because each URI has its own filter.

**Fix.**
- `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment`: up to three roles still get one filtered request each. For more than three, it reads each endpoint once with no role filter (paged and cached, so other checks can reuse it) and keeps only the requested roles. When a caller passes `-Select`, it adds `roleDefinitionId` so the local filter works. This is the same pattern the Zero Trust Assessment uses for its role export.
- New internal helper `Get-MtRoleUserSyncStatus -RoleId`: returns the user members of the given roles with `onPremisesSyncEnabled`, and throws if Graph leaves out a user or the field. CIS.M365.1.1.1 and CISA.MS.AAD.7.3 now share this Graph lookup. Each check still passes its own benchmark's set of roles: CIS uses the administrative roles and Global Reader, and CISA uses Global Administrator, as before. CISA.MS.AAD.7.3 now gets the same checks for missing data that CIS already had.
- The Zero Trust Assessment pack: ZTA.21814 (Privileged accounts are cloud native identities) now lists CIS.M365.1.1.1 under `AlsoCheckedBy`, and `catalog.json` was regenerated with `build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1` against ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0. The change has no runtime dependency on the ZTA module or its database.

This is a bug fix, so it fits the 3.0 code freeze.

content.text:
CodeRabbit found a real bug in [maester365/maester#2684](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2684); I fixed it and pushed the fix (commit `df8c9e97a`).

**The bug:** setting `AssignmentType` on each assignment also overwrote Graph's own `assignmentType` field, because PowerShell treats the two names as the same property. The session cache hands back those same objects, so any later caller of the same request got `Active` where Graph had returned `Assigned`. This already happened when no roles were passed. My PR made it also happen whenever more than three roles are passed, which on P2 and Governance tenants is what CIS.M365.1.1.1 now does.

**The fix:** [Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1](../maester-role-perf/powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment.ps1) now copies each assignment before adding the property, which is what CodeRabbit suggested. A new unit test checks that the cached object keeps `assignmentType = 'Assigned'`; it fails without the fix and passes with it. 2,293 related tests pass with the fix, and the analyzer has no findings.

`Get-MtRoleMember` still adds `AssignmentType` straight onto the principal objects, which are also shared with the cache. Graph's user and group objects don't have that field, so nothing of Graph's gets overwritten. But a user who holds two roles keeps whichever `AssignmentType` was written last. That behaviour predates this PR and I left it alone.
